serp_competitors.title: Compare Broadband Deals August 2026
serp_competitors.observed_structure: Large postcode-first comparison tool with address refinement, social-tariff control, provider-coverage disclosure, customer-service methodology and extensive explanatory help.
serp_competitors.content_gap_to_improve: Give users a provider shortlist before the address-level deal step and make the limits of provider coverage estimates explicit without claiming whole-market completeness.
serp_competitors.useful_ux_patterns: Postcode first, address refinement, social-tariff inclusion and clear explanations when results are incomplete.
serp_competitors.useful_ui_patterns: Prominent form, progressive eligibility states, filters and visible methodology links.
serp_competitors.interactive_or_functional_elements: Postcode and address lookup, result filters and social-tariff option.
serp_competitors.trust_signals: Named methodology, coverage limitations, provider inclusion disclosure and regularly refreshed deal data.
serp_competitors.citation_patterns: Methodology and provider coverage statements appear next to the tool rather than being hidden in generic terms.

serp_competitors.title: Which? Switch Broadband
serp_competitors.observed_structure: Deal cards lead with price, average speed, contract length, price-rise treatment and customer score, followed by a practical guide to choosing and switching.
serp_competitors.content_gap_to_improve: Offer a neutral provider-level shortlist across national and local networks, then direct users to exact-address checks rather than presenting sample deals as universally available.
serp_competitors.useful_ux_patterns: Show decision-critical figures together and explain why total cost and household needs matter.
serp_competitors.useful_ui_patterns: Scannable deal cards, expert answer block, step sequence and strong headings.
serp_competitors.interactive_or_functional_elements: Postcode comparison, provider filters and deal-level actions.
serp_competitors.trust_signals: Named expert, customer score methodology, commercial-cost breakdown and update context.
serp_competitors.citation_patterns: Regulatory switching claims are paired with practical advice and identifiable expert commentary.

ai_overview.observation: The UK search response checked on 23 August 2026 did not expose an AI Overview for the exact primary query. No overview citations were available to inspect. The page is therefore structured for extractable answers and entity clarity without claiming AI Overview inclusion.

research_summary: Current UK results favour postcode-led tools supported by transparent deal ordering, cost explanations, speed guidance, switching help and FAQs. The strongest pages state coverage limits and commercial methodology. BroadbandPicker can differentiate through its saved two-to-three-provider shortlist, clear separation between provider-level starting figures and exact-address offers, and current Ofcom evidence placed beside the decision it supports.
depth_rationale: The reviewed ranking pages range from roughly 1,800 to more than 4,000 words because the broad commercial query combines provider discovery, local availability, price, speed, contract, service and switching intent. A minimum of 1,800 useful words is appropriate when the interactive table remains central and the supporting copy answers each decision question without duplicating individual provider reviews.
